jv_partners: Caisse de Dépôt et de Gestion (CDG, Morocco)
research_notes: Africa's first battery cell gigafactory, in Kenitra (Atlantic coast), northwest Morocco. Investment agreement signed with the Moroccan government in June 2024; total commitment reported at USD 5.6–6.5bn across five development phases. Site preparation/earthworks completed and full construction launched around May 2025 — hence status = under_construction. Production start slated for Q3 2026 at 20 GWh (phase 1, ~USD 1.3bn, 156 ha); government-approved expansion to 40 GWh in phase 2, reaching an eventual full nameplate of 100 GWh across all five phases (phase timing beyond phase 1 not precisely dated, so capacity_ref_year left null). Operating entity is Gotion Power Morocco, a partnership between Gotion High-Tech and Morocco's state investment fund CDG (jv_partners). Site makes lithium-ion cells and packs plus cathode material (mixed cell + material site); Gotion produces both LFP and NMC, but the exact Kenitra chemistry/cell format is not separately confirmed for this plant. End markets: EV (targeting European OEMs incl. Renault/Stellantis in Morocco) and ESS — hence 'mixed'. Coordinates not confirmed for the specific site, so left null (Kenitra city only). Confidence 0.7: consistent across multiple reputable news/trade sources but not a primary company IR filing, and several figures (capacity phasing, chemistry) not company-confirmed at plant level.

No confirmed battery CELL manufacturing site for LG Energy Solution exists in Morocco. As of July 2024, LGES was only *considering* Morocco (alongside Finland and Indonesia) as a candidate site for a low-cost LFP EV-battery cell plant to serve an EU/EU-tariff-avoidance supply chain; no decision, location, capacity, or investment figure for a cell plant has been confirmed since. Hence is_cell_manufacturer=false and nameplate_capacity_gwh=null. LGES/LG Chem's CONCRETE Morocco investments are upstream material plants, NOT cells: (1) an LFP cathode materials plant (JV with China's Huayou/Youshan) targeting ~50,000 t/yr, start ~2026, for the North American IRA-eligible market; and (2) a lithium hydroxide refining plant (JV with China's Yahua Group), ~USD 612m Phase 1, ~30,000 t/yr. These are cathode/precursor and refining sites and fall outside the cell-manufacturing scope. Status set to 'announced' to reflect the mid-2024 consideration stage; confidence kept low (0.3) because the cell plant remains speculative and may not proceed. Chemistry noted as LFP per the stated low-cost LFP strategy. Coordinates unknown. Sources: Teslarati (2024-07-25), Morocco World News (2024-07), Yabiladi, C&EN, and metal.com/SMM coverage of the Huayou and Yahua material JVs.

Statevolt announced a US$3.2bn technology-agnostic battery CELL gigafactory in April 2024, located in RAKEZ's Al Hamra Industrial Zone, Ras Al Khaimah (60 hectare site). Operating entity is Statevolt Emirates. Full nameplate capacity up to 40 GWh/yr once fully ramped; initial production line ~6 GWh/yr targeted operational by end of 2026 (hence capacity_by_year_json {"2026":6}, nameplate 40). Chemistry: begins with semi-solid-state cells, planned transition to solid-state at full capacity. As of mid-2025 the project was awaiting permit approval and construction had not been confirmed, so status kept as 'announced' rather than under_construction. Target export markets: Africa, India, UAE and wider Middle East; automotive/EV-oriented but described as technology-agnostic, so end_market EV is tentative. Coordinates left null (only the Al Hamra Industrial Zone area is known, no precise sited figure). Cell format not disclosed. Not a JV of cell makers (partnership with RAK/RAKEZ), so jv_partners null. Confidence moderate: multiple reputable news sources (Investment Monitor, ETN News, Kallanish, Automotive Manufacturing Solutions) but an early-stage announced project with no confirmed construction/production and no official ramp schedule beyond the 6 GWh first line and 40 GWh eventual nameplate.

Announced Jan 2023: a ~AUD 300m lithium-ion battery CELL gigafactory at Avalon Airport, Geelong, Victoria, operated by Recharge Industries (parent Scale Facilitation, founder David Collard). Full nameplate target 30 GWh/yr; announced phased ramp of 2 GWh (H2 2024) then 6 GWh (2026) — recorded as null in capacity_by_year_json because none of these milestones were met. Technology partner Charge CCCV (C4V) providing IP; Accenture engaged for design/engineering. End market: EVs + stationary storage (mixed). PROJECT EFFECTIVELY STALLED/LIKELY DEFUNCT: as of mid-2023 reporting, no planning or environmental applications had been submitted, no lease was signed with land manager Linfox at Avalon, staff/contractors reportedly unpaid, and Scale Facilitation was raided by Australia's Serious Financial Crime Taskforce. Recharge redeployed staff to its UK Britishvolt/Cambois project, pausing the Australian venture. Kept status = 'announced' (never reached construction). Coordinates left null: the specific plant site was never secured/leased (intended location Avalon Airport, Geelong). No production ever commenced. Confidence lowered to 0.5 given the project's uncertain/likely-abandoned state; latest publicly available reporting predates 2024. is_cell_manufacturer set true as the site was intended to manufacture cells, though it was never built. Sources: pv magazine Australia (2023-01-17), innovationaus.com and pv magazine (2023-06) on stall/no lease/financial crime taskforce.

Site at Tomago, NSW, Australia ("Renaissance One", ~4,500 sqm). Operational since 2022. IMPORTANT: as currently operating, this facility ASSEMBLES battery packs/energy-storage systems ("superStorage", LFP chemistry) from imported cells - it is NOT yet a cell manufacturer, so is_cell_manufacturer=false. Stated production capacity is up to 300 MWh/yr initially, scaling to 5.3 GWh/yr at full nameplate (these figures are battery-SYSTEM/pack output, not confirmed cell output). Lithium-ion CELL manufacturing was announced as a separate second facility, "Renaissance Two", planned on the same Tomago site - that would make it a cell manufacturer, but Renaissance Two appears to remain at the announced/planning stage per available sources (no confirmed cell-production start). Chemistry LFP per company product descriptions. End market primarily stationary ESS (commercial/industrial), with some defence/transport applications (effectively mixed). Coordinates left null to avoid inventing a precise site location (Tomago locality, Port Stephens LGA, NSW). Capacity_ref_year and phased ramp JSON left null - no source pins the 300 MWh / 5.3 GWh figures to specific calendar years. Cross-checked pv magazine Australia, Energy-Storage.News, RenewEconomy and company site. Confidence lowered because the operational site is pack assembly while the cell-manufacturing element (Renaissance Two) is announced-only.

Pilot/small-scale cell manufacturing line established by Gelion at Battery Energy's existing lead-acid battery factory in Fairfield, Western Sydney, NSW. Produces Gelion's gel-based non-flow zinc-bromide "Endure" cells for stationary storage (6-12 hour duration), reusing ~70% of legacy lead-acid production processes. Launched 30 September 2022 (attended by federal ministers Bowen and Husic). Nameplate capacity ~2 MWh/year (0.002 GWh/yr) - a pilot line, not a gigafactory. It does manufacture actual cells (zinc-bromide), so counts as a cell manufacturer. IMPORTANT CAVEAT: The Gelion-Battery Energy partnership was subsequently wound down and Gelion pivoted to lithium-sulfur / silicon-sulfur R&D (ARENA-funded prototyping centre); the Fairfield Endure line's current operational status is uncertain and may be discontinued - status marked operational reflects confirmed 2022 production but confidence is lowered accordingly. Coordinates not precisely sourced (Fairfield, Western Sydney), left null. Region Australia = Rest of World.

Early-stage announcement. In July 2024, Bravo Motor Company Brasil Energy signed a Protocol of Intent / MoU with the Government of Bahia and the Municipality of Sao Sebastiao do Passe (Bahia state, NE Brazil) for what it bills as Latin America's first lithium battery cell gigafactory, producing cells for EVs and BESS. The project moved from Nova Lima, Minas Gerais to Bahia after disputes with Minas authorities.

Capacity: first phase ("Colossus Cluster") ~1 GWh/yr, valued at ~R$600m (~US$109m), ramping to 5 GWh/yr by 2028 per BMC's Jose E Marques. nameplate_capacity_gwh set to the sourced 5 GWh/yr 2028 target. Company also floated a much larger long-term vision of three clusters of ~35 GWh each (~105 GWh) and a stated ~R$25bn / nine-year total investment plan, but these are aspirational and unbacked by construction milestones - not used as nameplate. Land: ~400,000 sqm donated near ports/roads.

Status = announced: sources describe an MoU/protocol and "early planning phase"; no confirmation of construction start or operations as of mid-2024 reporting.

Chemistry stated only as "lithium battery cells" - specific chemistry (LFP/NMC) not confirmed. cell_format not disclosed.

Partners ABB, Rockwell Automation and SMC are named as automation/technology suppliers, not equity JV partners, so jv_partners left null.

Coordinates: only the municipality (Sao Sebastiao do Passe, Bahia) is known, not the exact plot; left null rather than guess. Corroborating trade coverage: bestmag.co.uk, fleetmobilitytoday.com, Revista Mineracao (2024-07-09), AutoData (2024-07-18). Founder: Argentine entrepreneur Miguel Angel Bravo. Confidence moderate: multiple trade-press sources but a nascent, MoU-stage project with shifting/aspirational figures.

PowerCap is a Brisbane / south-east Queensland based sodium-ion battery company. Multiple reputable sources (pv magazine Australia, RenewEconomy, ess-news, Energy Storage News) consistently state that PowerCap MAKES AND ASSEMBLES battery MODULES/PACKS in Queensland but OUTSOURCES CELL MANUFACTURE. Therefore the Queensland site is pack/module assembly, NOT a battery cell plant, so is_cell_manufacturer=false. The company is only "investigating"/"considering" future dedicated CELL manufacturing plants in the US (near customers) and India (to avoid trade tariffs); those are not yet announced sites and are not in Queensland. The frequently cited "5 GWh" figure refers to module ASSEMBLY capacity in Australia, not cell manufacturing capacity, so nameplate_capacity_gwh is left null to avoid mixing assembly and cell figures. Chemistry is sodium-ion (marketed as using recycled plastics, bio-waste, and sodium from desalination). Flagship product 'PowerCap POD' residential home energy storage system unveiled 4 December 2024; also targets commercial/US customers. Queensland assembly operation is operational (product launched and shipping); European market launch (Italy, Germany, Spain) Sept 2025, US entry Oct 2025. No specific street address or coordinates confirmed (Brisbane HQ / SE Queensland only). Confidence kept moderate/low because this is an assembly site rather than a confirmed cell-manufacturing gigafactory.

Phase 3 pilot/pre-commercial cell production facility in Geelong, Victoria (Deakin University precinct, Waurn Ponds), officially opened by Federal Industry Minister Ed Husic in August 2024; first cells produced 2024. Nameplate is a small 2 MWh/year (0.002 GWh/yr) automated pouch-cell line - described as Australia's largest such facility, housed in Australia's largest battery dry room. Genuine CELL manufacturer: full process from cathode powder creation/coating to cell fabrication and testing. Chemistry is lithium-sulfur / semi-solid-state Li-S plus lithium-metal; company reports ~498 Wh/kg first-discharge on 10Ah cells. End markets are lightweight high-energy-density applications (defence, aerospace, drones/UAVs, e-mobility) rather than mass EV/ESS - marked 'mixed'. Coordinates left null (not confirmed to a precise source). NOTE: separate/larger plans exist that should NOT be conflated with this site: a planned standalone 200MWh (0.2 GWh/yr) commercial 'Phase 4' facility (announced Nov 2023, location not tied to Geelong) and an ARENA-supported feasibility/FEED study (Nov 2025, ~US$7.9m grant) for an eventual up-to-1 GWh/yr giga-scale plant - both distinct future projects, not the operational Geelong line. Sources: lis.energy Phase 3 opening; pv-magazine-australia (2024-02-09 scale-up, 2025-11-18 ARENA funding); PPK Group Phase 3 demo; ARENA project page; lis.energy 200MWh announcement.

plant_name: Sodium Batteries Australia pilot manufacturing facility
research_notes: Sodium Batteries Australia describes itself as a sovereign Australian manufacturer of sodium-ion (Na-ion) batteries for stationary residential, industrial and grid-scale (ESS) applications. Per the company website, it operates a 1MW pilot Na-ion manufacturing facility (stated as operational) and has plans for 2 x >1GW large-scale production facilities. Confirmed via company website snippet and multiple search corroborations that it manufactures cells (not just packs). KEY UNCERTAINTIES: (1) Plant location not disclosed in any source found — city/state and coordinates unknown. (2) "1MW pilot" is a power rating for the demonstration line, not an annual GWh/year cell-manufacturing throughput; no credible GWh/year nameplate figure was sourced, so nameplate_capacity_gwh left null. (3) The 2 x >1GW facilities are announced/planned only, not built — do not conflate with the operational pilot. (4) No announced_year or start_year confirmed by a source. The company website returned HTTP 403 to direct fetch; details rely on search-result snippets of sodiumbatteriesau.com plus corroborating trade press (ess-news, pv-magazine). plant_name: Allegro Energy Warners Bay (pilot line at The Melt, Dashworks)
research_notes: Warners Bay is Allegro Energy's PILOT-scale manufacturing line, located at "The Melt" (a manufacturing incubator) at Dashworks, Warners Bay, New South Wales. Commissioned early 2023, it produces supercapacitors and the aqueous microemulsion electrolyte/components for Allegro's water-based redox flow batteries (non-flammable, no vanadium/lithium). This is NOT a gigafactory and NOT a conventional Li-ion cell plant. Allegro's headquarters is at Thornton, NSW. The company's stated plan is to build its FIRST GIGAFACTORY later (location undecided, "ideally in Australia"); Origin Energy holds an equity stake with an option to fund that gigafactory - this pilot line is a separate, earlier facility. No annual manufacturing throughput (GWh/yr) is publicly sourced for the Warners Bay line, so nameplate_capacity_gwh is left null. Note: the widely-cited "60 MWh" figure refers to a planned deployment at Origin's Eraring power station (a flow-battery project), NOT the manufacturing capacity of this site - deliberately excluded to avoid mixing deployment with manufacturing capacity. is_cell_manufacturer set true because the site fabricates energy-storage cells (flow/supercapacitor) at pilot scale, though it is borderline vs. the database's gigafactory scope given it is pilot-only. Coordinates left null (only suburb-level location known; exact site address not sourced). Corroborating sources: pv-magazine (2025-03-28) on microemulsion flow battery unveiling; ess-news / pv-magazine (2024-09-10) on A$17.5m Series A capacity ramp; themelt.io Allegro case study.

chemistry: chemistry-agnostic (3D current collectors / electrodes for Li-ion, LFP, NMC, solid-state)
research_notes: NOT a battery cell manufacturer. Addionics is an Israeli startup (founded 2018) that produces "Smart 3D Electrodes" and 3D-structured current collectors (aluminium and copper) — a battery COMPONENT, not finished cells. Its technology is chemistry-agnostic and sold to cell/OEM partners; the site does not manufacture complete battery cells, so is_cell_manufacturer=false. Pilot line inaugurated Feb 2023, ~1,500 sq m, also serving as HQ in Tel Aviv, Israel (Menachem Begin 82). Reported capacity figures (up to 1 MWh initially, targeting ~100 MWh by end-2024 and ~1 GWh during 2025) refer to ELECTRODE/current-collector output, not annual cell nameplate capacity — therefore nameplate_capacity_gwh left null to avoid conflating a component figure with cell GWh/yr. Note: Addionics has since announced a first US manufacturing facility (separate site, ~$39m raise); this record covers only the Israel pilot line. Precise coordinates not confirmed to street level, left null. Sources: BusinessWire (2023-02-26), Israel Defense, DigiTimes, ISRAEL21c, Forbes, Latitude Media.

Afrivolt (formerly Aqora) announced plans in January 2024 for its first lithium-ion cell gigafactory ("Afrivolt 1") at the Atlantis Special Economic Zone for Green Technologies near Cape Town, Western Cape. Plan: start with a 1.5 GWh modular line using imported cell materials, expandable to an ultimate nameplate of 5 GWh; site is intended to produce cells (and anodes/cathodes) initially for stationary storage (ESS) and, in the medium term, for EVs — hence end_market recorded as mixed. As of the June 2024 update the project was still in feasibility/due-diligence and financing stage (talks with finance institutions, European feasibility studies, ReElement/American Resources Corporation named as an offtake partner) — no confirmed construction start, no groundbreaking, no dated ramp schedule, so status = announced and start_year, capacity_ref_year and capacity_by_year_json left null. nameplate_capacity_gwh set to the eventual 5 GWh full nameplate. Exact plant coordinates not published; Atlantis SEZ is ~40 km north of central Cape Town, but no confirmed site coordinates so lat/long left null. Cell chemistry not specified in sources (Li-ion). Confidence 0.6: single/consistent reputable trade-press source (Engineering News/Creamer Media), plausible and specific, but early-stage and no primary company financials confirmed.

Salient Energy is a Canadian startup headquartered in Dartmouth, Nova Scotia, developing water-based zinc-ion cells (zinc anode, manganese-oxide-based cathode, pH-neutral zinc sulphate electrolyte) for stationary/residential energy storage. This is the company's HQ and pilot cell manufacturing line. As of April 2022 the Dartmouth facility produced ~100 batteries per month, with plans to ramp to pilot scale (1000s/month). This is a genuine cell manufacturer (zinc-ion cells), but at pilot/pre-commercial scale, not a gigawatt-scale plant — no GWh nameplate figure is published, so nameplate_capacity_gwh is left null. The separate planned "first gigafactory" (location TBD, USA or Canada, targeted ~2024/2025) is a distinct future project, not this Dartmouth site. Company remained active into 2025 (awarded a California Energy Commission grant to demonstrate a 10 kWh residential Zn-ion ESS). Coordinates not confirmed to a specific site, left null. Status "operational" reflects the running pilot line, though confidence is moderate given sources are dated 2022. Region kept as Rest of World (Canada).

jv_partners: Megamillion Energy Group, Dr Henry Mao (Chinese battery manufacturing team)
research_notes: Planned "Africa's first" lithium-ion battery cell gigafactory, branded Giga-Africa 1. Sited in the Coega Special Economic Zone near Gqeberha (Port Elizabeth), Eastern Cape, South Africa (multiple sources: greenbuildingafrica, energymixreport, engineeringnews). First announced Feb 2020 (CleanTechnica) with a master plan to scale to 32 GWh/year of cells by 2028; re-launched Feb/Apr 2025 as a JV between Megamillion and Chinese battery expert Dr Henry Mao (described as "father of Li-ion manufacturing in China", 182 patents), who would transfer technology, equipment and staff in phases. Plan: initial ~1 GWh/year, scaling to 32 GWh/year full nameplate by 2028. Serves both stationary energy storage (ESS) and mobility/EV markets, hence end_market=mixed. Chemistry reported as LFP (Energize: "SA's first LFP battery gigafactory"). IS a cell manufacturer, but note phased approach: initially "dry cells" produced in China with electrolyte-filling and post-processing done in South Africa, ramping toward full local cell manufacture. Status kept as 'announced' — as of a March 2026 IOL report the project was still at feasibility/viability-study stage, not confirmed under construction. Exact plant coordinates within the ~400 ha Coega site not confirmed, so lat/long left null. capacity_by_year_json holds only the sourced 2028 full-nameplate figure; the ~1 GWh initial-phase timing is not firmly dated. Primary sources returned HTTP 403 to direct fetch; details corroborated across CI Live, MarkLines, Green Building Africa, Energy Mix Report and Engineering News via search summaries. Note a separate, unrelated 2020-era Coega Li-ion effort and Cape Town's Balancell exist — this record is specifically the Megamillion/Mao gigafactory.

e-Zinc is a Toronto-headquartered long-duration energy storage (LDES) company. Its production site named in the candidate list ("e-Zinc Toronto") is actually a 42,000 sq ft PILOT manufacturing facility at 7391 Pacific Circle, Mississauga (Malton), Ontario, which opened with a ceremony on 23 Oct 2024 and serves as its Canadian HQ housing Operations, Engineering and R&D. Financed by a USD $31M Series A2 round (led by Evok Innovations; investors include Mitsubishi Heavy Industries, Export Development Canada, Ultratech Capital Partners; ~CAD $42M total). The technology stores energy electrochemically in zinc metal (zinc-air), targeting 24-hour (long-duration) storage — NOT conventional Li-ion cells. It IS a cell/electrochemical-device manufacturer but at PILOT/demonstration scale only; the facility focuses on building pilot demonstration systems and replicable assembly processes ahead of scaled manufacturing, with some downstream cell assembly/integration relying on third-party suppliers. No GWh/year nameplate capacity is publicly disclosed, so nameplate_capacity_gwh left null. Precise lat/long not confirmed from a source, left null (address: 7391 Pacific Circle, Mississauga, ON). Note this is a flow/zinc LDES technology, an outlier vs the Li-ion gigafactory scope. Sources: e-Zinc press/blog, Canadian Manufacturing, BetaKit, SustainableBiz (Oct 2024). Confidence moderate: status/site well-sourced, but capacity and coordinates unconfirmed.

jv_partners: YPF, CONICET, Universidad Nacional de La Plata (UNLP)
research_notes: UniLiB (first National Plant for Technological Development of Lithium Cells and Batteries) in La Plata, Buenos Aires province, is a JV of Y-TEC (YPF's technology company, itself an YPF-CONICET JV) and the Universidad Nacional de La Plata (UNLP), located at the "Jorge Alberto Sabato" tech-productive pole. It is described as the first lithium cell & battery plant in Latin America. IMPORTANT: this is a pilot/development-scale plant, NOT a gigafactory. It genuinely manufactures LFP (lithium iron phosphate) lithium-ion CELLS, so is_cell_manufacturer=true. Nameplate capacity is only ~13-15 MWh/year (i.e. ~0.013-0.015 GWh/yr); I recorded 0.015 GWh/yr — orders of magnitude below commercial gigafactories. Equivment cited as ~1,000 stationary batteries or 400 EVs / 2,500 homes; designed ~300 cells/day per 8-hour shift. Cells target both stationary renewable storage (ESS) and electric vehicles/buses, hence end_market=mixed. Status: equipment installed and start-up/inauguration reported late 2023, entering production — treated as operational; start_year=2023. announced_year ~2021 (approximate, lower confidence). Total investment cited ~USD 7 million. Coordinates left null (UNLP campus, Diagonal 113 between 64 and 66, La Plata) as no precise site coordinate was sourced; did not guess. Separately, Y-TEC/YPF has announced a much larger future industrial gigafactory — that is a distinct project and not this pilot site. Sources: UNLP institutional pages, CONICET La Plata, Infobae (2023-10-17), Buenos Aires Herald.

plant_name: LG Energy Solution Ochang Energy Plant
chemistry: NMC/NCA (cylindrical); LFP line from 2027; semi-solid-state pilot
research_notes: Ochang Energy Plant in Ochang-eup, Cheongju, North Chungcheong Province, South Korea (~130 km south of Seoul). LG Energy Solution's flagship domestic "mother factory" and R&D/production hub for its entire product portfolio. Opened 2004 (batteries for e-bikes/laptops), producing EV cells since 2011. Confirmed operational cell manufacturer. Flagship 2170 cylindrical cells supplied to Tesla; started 46-Series (4680) cylindrical mass production 2024 (4680 line ~9 GWh, 2170 line +4 GWh). Total site capacity cited at ~35 GWh after expansions (post-2022/2026 expansion basis) - treat as approximate; sources do not cleanly separate operational-now vs planned nameplate, hence confidence 0.6. LGES investing ~KRW 4tn (~$3.1bn) in Ochang expansion through 2026, plus a new domestic LFP line (initial 1 GWh, scalable) targeted for 2027 and a semi-solid-state pilot line. Coordinates not found in a citable source, left null. Primary formats cylindrical but as mother factory it develops all formats/chemistries. End market primarily EV, also ESS. Key sources: electrive (2022, 4680), KED Global (2023, mother factory), Korea Herald (LFP 2027).

chemistry: NMC (adding LFP for ESS; solid-state and sodium-ion lines planned)
research_notes: Samsung SDI's original/home battery cell plant, located in Ulju-gun (Samnam-myeon), Ulsan, South Korea. EV battery mass production began 2011; the site produces medium-to-large prismatic NCM/NMC cells with an annual capacity reported at ~10 GWh (ref ~2024). Multiple sources (Korea Herald / The Investor, Aug 2025) report Samsung SDI is installing LFP cell production equipment for ESS on the Ulsan 'mother line', targeting large-scale LFP-for-ESS output by late 2025/2026; these LFP cells feed the company's Michigan (USA) pack facility. Samsung SDI has announced a ~16 trillion won (part of ~25 trillion won 2026-2040) investment programme to build mass-production lines for all-solid-state, LFP-ESS and sodium-ion batteries at the Ulsan complex. Site is a cell manufacturer (not pack-only). Chemistry recorded as NMC today with LFP/solid-state/sodium-ion expansion. End market mixed (EV + ESS). Nameplate 10 GWh is a single-source/tracker figure, hence moderate confidence. Coordinates not confirmed from a reliable source, left null to avoid invention. Original Korea Herald source returned HTTP 403 on direct fetch but content was captured via search summary; The Investor (theinvestor.co.kr/article/10410828) carries the same reporting.

chemistry: mixed (Li-ion NMC/NCA small-format cells and 46-series cylindrical; solid-state / next-gen validation)
research_notes: Long-established Samsung SDI cell plant at 467 Beonyeong-ro, Seobuk-gu, Cheonan-si, Chungcheongnam-do. Historically the core site for "small-sized" batteries (cylindrical and pouch Li-ion for smartphones, tablets, notebooks, power tools) and Samsung SDI's flagship "mother factory" for process/tech validation. The pilot "M Line" for small-format cells began operating June 2018. A 4680 cylindrical pilot line was announced June 2022 with ~1 GWh initial capacity, expandable to 8-12 GWh (electrive). Mass production of next-gen 46-series (46-phi, e.g. 4695) cylindrical cells began at Cheonan in March 2025, with initial supply to a US customer (Samsung SDI newsroom). In July 2026, Samsung SDI announced a ~25 trillion won next-gen battery investment split between Ulsan and Cheonan, with roughly 9 trillion won for Cheonan; Cheonan is positioned as the R&D "mother factory" that validates next-gen chemistries while Ulsan is the mass-production base for all-solid-state, LFP and sodium cells (solid-state mass production targeted 2H 2027 at Ulsan). No reliable single annual nameplate GWh figure exists for Cheonan (it is a mixed R&D + small-format cell site), so nameplate_capacity_gwh left null. Coordinates not left as a sourced precise value (approx central Cheonan) so latitude/longitude left null to avoid guessing. Sources: Samsung SDI newsroom (samsungsdi.com/sdi-now/sdi-news/4322.html, 2025-03-31); electrive (2022 4680 pilot, 2025 46-series); The Elec / Korea JoongAng Daily / techtimes on the 2026 Ulsan-Cheonan investment split; Samsung SDI global network page for site location.

Giheung (150-20 Gongse-ro, Giheung-gu, Yongin-si, Gyeonggi-do) is Samsung SDI's corporate headquarters and R&D/administrative centre, not a dedicated battery cell manufacturing plant. As of 2026, Samsung SDI's domestic (Korean) cell manufacturing is at Ulsan (mid/large cells, LFP ESS, all-solid-state, sodium-ion mass-production lines) and Cheonan (mother line, DryEV pilot dry-electrode line, R&D); its solid-state pilot line is in Suwon. Sources consistently place battery R&D and development activity at Giheung/Yongin but describe it as HQ/admin rather than a volume cell plant, so is_cell_manufacturer set false. No sourced current cell-manufacturing nameplate capacity, status, chemistry, or cell format could be confirmed specifically for Giheung, so those fields are left null. Coordinates left null to avoid guessing (approx. area of Yongin, Gyeonggi-do). Confidence low due to residual uncertainty about any legacy small-cell activity. Sources: Samsung SDI global network page (HTTP 403 on direct fetch, referenced via search); Wikipedia (Samsung SDI HQ in Giheung-gu, Yongin); TechTimes / The Elec (2026) on the 25 trillion won Ulsan+Cheonan next-gen battery investment split identifying those as the production sites.

SK On's domestic (Seosan Auto Valley, South Chungcheong Province) battery cell plant. First line commissioned 2012 (~0.2 GWh); second line 2018 brought the site to ~5 GWh/yr, its capacity through 2024. In Aug 2023 SK On announced a KRW 1.5tn (~$1.1bn) investment to add a third production line (online 2025, ramping to ~14 GWh added by 2028), quadrupling domestic capacity from 5 GWh to ~20 GWh/yr by 2028; existing lines also upgraded to smart factories. Chemistry is NMC (NCM) pouch cells for EVs; from H2 2026 the site is slated to mass-produce Korea's first EREV (NCM pouch) batteries for Hyundai/Genesis. Overall site is operational with expansion in progress; nameplate 20 GWh is the eventual 2028 figure. Coordinates not confirmed from a source, left null. Capacity_by_year is approximate: 2025 value (10) is an interpolated ramp point between the confirmed 5 GWh (through 2024) and ~20 GWh (2028); confirmed anchors are 0.2 (2012), 5 (2018/2024) and 20 (2028). Sources: KED Global (2023-08-16), electrive (2023-08-21), Seoul Economic Daily (2026-05).

plant_name: CATL CATIB Karawang Battery Cell Plant
operator: PT Contemporary Amperex Technology Indonesia Battery (CATIB)
jv_partners: CATL (via CBL, 70%), Indonesia Battery Corporation (IBC, 30%, backed by Antam/PLN/Pertamina/Inalum)
research_notes: Battery cell + module plant at Karawang, West Java (KNIC / Artha Industrial Hill), part of CATL's ~US$6bn Indonesia Battery Integration Project spanning nickel mining, materials, cells and recycling. JV PT CATIB signed 16 Oct 2024: CATL subsidiary CBL 70%, Indonesia's IBC 30%. Groundbreaking 29 June 2025 (President Prabowo attending). plant_name: HLI Green Power Karawang Battery Cell Plant

research_notes: JV between Hyundai Motor Group, LG Energy Solution and Indonesia Battery Corporation (IBC); operated by PT HLI Green Power. research_notes:
EVE Energy's first production base outside China (its 53rd plant), located in the Kulim district / Padang Serai (KEIP), Kedah, Malaysia. NOT a JV - wholly-owned by EVE Energy; Invest Kedah is the state investment-promotion partner (MoU signatory for the Phase II land), not an equity partner.

Phase I - "International Cylindrical Battery Industry Park": 15 production lines, ~684 million 21700-format cylindrical Li-ion cells/yr, equivalent to just over 10 GWh/yr, for power tools and electric two-wheelers. Investment ~USD 420-422m. Construction began Aug 2023; equipment-installation ceremony Dec 2024; first cell off the line Feb 2025 (now operational).

Phase II - energy storage (LFP) batteries, planned ~10 GWh/yr (some reports 10-15 GWh); Phase II reported completed/entering large-scale production ~26 Feb 2026 (Gasgoo/AfMA/Just-Auto).

Capacity: I recorded nameplate ~20 GWh/yr (2026) = Phase I ~10 GWh (operational 2025) + Phase II ~10 GWh (2026). Multiple sources agree on location, ~10 GWh Phase I cylindrical, and operational status; capacity totals across phases are less certain, hence confidence 0.78.

chemistry=LFP inferred from REPT's LFP/BESS product focus (strongly indicated but not stated as LFP for this specific line in the sources found). cell_format=prismatic inferred from REPT's flagship large-format prismatic (Wending) BESS cells — not explicitly sourced for this plant. Specific plant location (city/province) not confirmed; Jakarta references relate to the ICEE expo, not the factory site — coordinates left null. First LFP battery CELL factory in Vietnam, located in Vung Ang Economic Zone, Ha Tinh (Ky Anh district). JV owned 51% Gotion High-Tech / 49% VinES (Vingroup). Groundbreaking November 2022; total investment ~VND 6,329bn (~USD 275m); site ~14 ha; design capacity 5 GWh/year (~30 million cells/year). Mass production was targeted for Q3 2024, revised from an initial end-2023 target. As of the latest available reporting I could not find a primary source confirming that mass production actually began, so status is kept as under_construction and start_year 2024 is a target, not a confirmed date. Primarily serves VinFast EVs (closed-loop LFP supply alongside VinES pack plant at Vung Ang). Cell format not confirmed by sources; exact factory coordinates not confirmed, left null. Capacity/JV structure cross-checked across Green Car Congress, Energy-Storage.News, Gotion IR and Vietnam News.

Amita Technology (Thailand), a subsidiary of Energy Absolute (EA), operates the first battery cell gigafactory in ASEAN, located on a ~90-rai plot in the Blue Tech City industrial estate, Bang Pakong district, Chachoengsao, within Thailand's Eastern Economic Corridor (EEC). Production began 12 December 2021. The plant manufactures lithium-ion pouch cells (marketed with ultra-fast-charge / ~3,000-cycle capability) serving both EV and energy-storage (ESS) markets. Capacity: initial ~1 GWh/yr operational, with phase 1 designed to expand to 4 GWh/yr (recorded as nameplate). EA has stated a long-term ambition to scale the site to 50 GWh/yr, and separately announced plans to set up additional battery-cell plants in Thailand with two Chinese partners (a distinct effort, not confirmed as this site's operator). Coordinates and precise NMC/LFP chemistry not confirmed by a primary source, so left null. Sources: Nation Thailand grand-opening release (nationthailand.com/pr-news/business/40009916), Nation Thailand (40010110, 40037092), Just Auto (just-auto.com/news/ea-completes-ev-battery-plant-in-thailand), APEC document (mddb.apec.org 22_ad2_012.pdf), MarkLines (marklines.com/en/global/10346).

This Sriracha (Chonburi) site is a battery MODULE and PACK ASSEMBLY plant, NOT a cell manufacturing facility - hence is_cell_manufacturer=false. SVOLT describes it as a "module and pack" plant with two lines (one producing HEV/PHEV/BEV modules, one assembling packs); capacity is stated as ~60,000 modules and packs per year (a UNIT figure, not a cell GWh capacity, so nameplate_capacity_gwh left null). The cells used are SVOLT's L600-series LFP short-blade prismatic cells imported from China (the first pack was a 60 kWh LFP/LCTP pack, 500+ km range). Timeline: construction began 5 July 2023; first pack off the line 20 Dec 2023; mass production began Feb 2024; 10,000th EV pack milestone reached 30 June 2025. Products supply Great Wall Motor (ORA, Haval, Tank) and Hozon in Thailand. JV: Banpu NEXT (subsidiary of Thai energy group Banpu) acquired shares in SVOLT Thailand; SVOLT retains operating control, so operator set to SVOLT with Banpu NEXT as JV partner. SVOLT initiated a feasibility study on LOCALIZED CELL PRODUCTION in Thailand from 2026 to meet local-content policy, but no cell line is confirmed operational as of research date. Exact coordinates not confirmed in sources; left null. Sources: CnEVPost (28 Feb 2024, mass production; 6 July 2023, construction start; 2 July 2025, 10,000th pack), Banpu NEXT press releases, SEAISI. If a localized cell line is confirmed, this row's is_cell_manufacturer and capacity should be revisited.

Production ramps in phases: battery modules using imported cells from ~Q3 2026, with full cell-level production expected Q1 2027 (hence start_year=2027; the site is currently under construction/ramping as of mid-2026). Capacity/chemistry from single-tracker reporting (electrification-solutions, ess-news, CnEVPost), status and investment corroborated by BOI/PR Newswire release — hence confidence 0.65. Original AESC/Nissan pouch-cell plant at 500 Battery Plant Rd, Smyrna, TN (adjacent to the Nissan Smyrna assembly plant); established 2012 to supply NMC pouch cells for the Nissan LEAF. Owned by Nissan, then majority-acquired by China's Envision Group in 2018 (Nissan retained ~25%). Nissan/EV cell production ceased mid-2025 and the ~550,000 sq ft, 500+ employee site was retooled during 2025 to make lithium-iron-phosphate (LFP) cells for stationary energy storage — described as the first LFP ESS cell manufacturing facility in the US, with ~3 GWh/year annual capacity. On 1 April 2026 Fixx Energy took majority control of the plant (sale done to comply with the One Big Beautiful Bill Act / FEOC rules); Fixx signed multi-year agreements to supply cells to Fluence (AESC had also signed a 10 GWh BESS cell/module deal with Prevalon). Chemistry now LFP (historically NMC). Cell format left null: AESC heritage is laminated pouch but the current ESS cell format is not confirmed. start_year=2012 is the site's first production; LFP/ESS production began 2025. Coordinates are approximate, geocoded from the confirmed street address. source_date is the access date; the ownership-change article is dated May 2026.

LFP battery CELL gigafactory in Tucson, Arizona (Aerospace Research Campus, ~267 acres, south of Tucson International Airport). Site selected Dec 2022; ceremonial groundbreaking Oct 2023; vertical construction slated to begin mid-2026 following financing closure enabled by offtake deals; production expected late 2027, full initial run rate in 2028. Initial nameplate 5.5 GWh/yr (incl. a 0.5 GWh R&D line), designed to scale to ~15 GWh/yr on the same site; some earlier reporting cited a longer-term 20 GWh target (no timeline). In March 2026 ABF announced >4.5 GWh of binding offtake from undisclosed 'A-rated' ESS companies covering most of the initial 5.5 GWh output for the first five years, so end market is primarily stationary storage (ESS). Chemistry is LFP; cell format reported as prismatic (moderate confidence). Status set to under_construction but is borderline (financing was being finalised around mid-2026); if construction had not physically started it is closer to 'announced'. Parent/backer commonly reported as Lion Energy (Utah-based); equipment partner is Wuxi Lead (LEAD). No precise coordinates published, so latitude/longitude left null. capacity_ref_year left null as the 15 GWh full nameplate has no firm year; JSON shows the confirmed 5.5 GWh 2028 run rate. A separate ~$1.2B cathode/anode component plant reported for Tucson is a different (materials) facility and not this cell site. Some trackers cited a 30 GWh figure that conflates the materials-offtake context; not used here.

Battery cell gigafactory on the Huron Campus (former IBM site), 1093 Clark Street, Endicott, NY 13760. Manufactured lithium-ion phosphate (LFP / "P-Series" phosphate-based) cells for both EV and ESS/BESS markets. Construction completed mid-2022; commercial cell production began late 2022. Initial single line ~1 GWh/yr, ramping toward ~1.8 GWh/yr nameplate; longer-term expansion to 38 GWh by 2030 was announced but never realised. IMPORTANT CURRENT STATUS: the plant is effectively DEFUNCT. iM3NY shut the gigafactory and laid off its workforce in October 2024; iM3NY LLC / Imperium3 New York filed Chapter 11 bankruptcy on 27 January 2025 (District of Delaware). Assets were sold to Musashi Auto Parts for ~$10M and the Delaware case was dismissed in June 2025 with zero creditor recovery; the iM3NY sign was removed in 2025. Status recorded as 'operational' only because the schema offers no 'closed/defunct' value and the site did produce cells at commercial scale — it is NOT currently producing. iM3NY was a consortium/JV: majority owner Magnis Energy Technologies (Australia) with technology partner Charge CCCV (C4V). Cell format not reliably confirmed (left null). Coordinates are approximate site-level (Huron Campus, Endicott) — not confirmed to metre precision. Sources: im3ny.com/gigafactory, energy-storage.news (gigafactory opening), wbng.com/wskg.org/pipedream (bankruptcy & shutdown), chamberofcommerce.com (address).

$2bn facility in Manteno, Kankakee County, Illinois (along I-57), converting a former Kmart distribution center (~1.5M sq ft, ~150 acres). Plan is 40 GWh of LFP lithium-ion CELLS plus 10 GWh of battery packs; the 40 GWh cell figure is the eventual full nameplate, expected to be reached by ~2034 (capacity_ref_year=2034). nameplate_capacity_gwh reflects cell capacity only, excluding the separate 10 GWh pack line, per the cell-manufacturing scope. Announced ~September 2023; production began ramping in 2025 with five production lines operating and ~250-300 staff by late 2025 (S&P/AutotechInsight reported a September 2025 production start; Shaw Local Nov 2025 update), so classified operational (early ramp). Parent Gotion High-Tech (Guoxuan High-Tech); Volkswagen is Gotion High-Tech's largest shareholder but the Manteno site is wholly Gotion, not a plant-level JV. Chemistry LFP (confirmed). End market mixed: EV batteries plus energy storage system integration. cell_format not confirmed by a source, left null (Gotion LFP is typically prismatic). Coordinates are TOWN-LEVEL for Manteno, IL (~41.25, -87.83) — exact plant coordinates were not confirmed by a source; treat as approximate. capacity_by_year_json left null as no reliable year-by-year cell ramp figures were sourced. Sources: Manufacturing Dive, Construction Dive, InsideEVs (2023 announcement); S&P Global AutotechInsight and Shaw Local Daily Journal (2025 production status); gotionillinois.com.

chemistry: LFP (lithium iron phosphate); anode-free cells also planned
