It manufactures LFP cells (and planned anode-free cells) - a genuine cell manufacturer, not just pack/module assembly. Pilot LFP cell production began Oct/Nov 2023, so the site is operational at pilot/early scale, though the full 20 GWh build-out was paused amid funding difficulties. Company hit repeated layoffs (25% Nov 2023; more Mar 2024; ~45% workforce cut Jan 2026) and in Jan 2026 pivoted away from EV batteries toward rail, defence and utility-scale energy storage after losing an EV contract - so end_market has shifted from EV toward ESS/mixed. 20 GWh is the eventual full annual nameplate (capacity_ref_year 2027 = original full-scale target); no reliable phased year-by-year ramp figures available given the paused build-out, so capacity_by_year_json left null. Coordinates are approximate, geocoded from the sourced street address (42060 Ecorse Road, Van Buren Township, MI 48111); treat as ~site-level, not surveyed. cell_format not firmly sourced, left null. Sources: ONE company announcement (one.ai/news/onecircle - HTTP 403 on direct fetch but corroborated via search snippet), Michigan Gov. Whitmer press release (michigan.gov, 2022-10-05), Area Development, InsideEVs (20 GWh LFP), MichiganBusiness.org (first cell production Nov 2023), Detroit News / Crain's Detroit (2024 and Jan 2026 layoffs and EV-to-rail/defence pivot).

CANCELLED — never built. Announced March 2023: Amprius Technologies selected Brighton, Colorado for its first large-scale silicon-anode Li-ion cell "gigafactory" (~774,000–775,000 sq ft, leased April 2023). Planned phased build: initial 500 MWh, scalable to 5 GWh within the initial footprint and up to 10 GWh with additional acreage; ~$190M investment including a $50M US DOE cost-sharing grant. Targeted operational H1 2025 but that was never met — only pre-construction planning was completed (as of 31 Dec 2024), with construction contingent on funding. On 30 January 2026 Amprius terminated the Brighton lease in exchange for a one-time $20.0M payment, effectively ending the Colorado factory. Company has pivoted to a contract-manufacturing strategy: >2.0 GWh/yr of SiCore cell supply via global contract manufacturers plus expansion of its Fremont, CA pilot line to ~10 MWh. Status recorded as 'announced' because the site never progressed to construction and is now cancelled; is_cell_manufacturer=false because no cells were ever produced at this site. nameplate 5.0 GWh reflects the announced initial-footprint target (never realised); ramp/ref-year left null as the plant will not be built. Coordinates left null (no precise site address confirmed). Chemistry: Amprius silicon-anode lithium-ion (SiCore platform), high-energy pouch cells aimed at aviation/HAPS/drones, EVs and premium mobility (mixed end market). Sources: Amprius/BusinessWire and Colorado OEDIT press releases (2023-03-06), pv-magazine USA (2023-03-06); cancellation from Amprius SEC Form 10-Q FY2026 (period ending 2026-03-31) and FY2025 10-K.

Microvast's Clarksville, TN site (building purchased 2021, announced Feb 2021) is designed as a vertically integrated battery CELL manufacturing plant (cells, modules, packs), so is_cell_manufacturer=true. Chemistry pivoted from NMC to LFP in Q2 2024; Clarksville is positioned as Microvast's primary US LFP base for both commercial-vehicle EV and ESS markets (hence end_market=mixed). Designed initial capacity ~2.0 GWh/yr; 82-acre site allows future expansion cited up to ~8 GWh. Status is under_construction: construction was suspended in Q2 2024 due to financing constraints and, per the FY2025 10-K (period ending 31 Dec 2025), cell production had not begun — all of Microvast's ~3.5 GWh of active capacity remains at Huzhou, China. No confirmed production start_year (originally targeted 2022/2023, repeatedly delayed). Cell format recorded as pouch based on Microvast's established pouch-cell products (53.5Ah, 565Ah), moderate confidence. Coordinates not reliably sourced, left null. Corroborating sources: Microvast IR release on final construction phases; pv magazine (LFP ESS). nameplate 2.0 GWh reflects designed initial cell/module/pack line.

QuantumScape's San Jose site (HQ, 1730 Technology Drive, San Jose, CA 95110) is a solid-state battery CELL pilot/R&D production facility, not a commercial gigafactory. It manufactures lithium-metal, anode-free solid-state cells (QSE-5, ~5 Ah), so is_cell_manufacturer = true. The "Eagle Line" highly automated pilot cell production line (using QS's Cobra separator process) was inaugurated 4 February 2026, described as the foundation for future GWh-scale production by QS's technology-licensing partners (e.g. PowerCo/Volkswagen) — QS itself is pursuing a licensing model rather than owning gigafactories. The earlier QS-0 pilot plant was announced ~2021 with planned capacity of up to ~200,000 cells/year (units, NOT GWh) to supply test vehicles. No credible annual GWh nameplate figure exists for this pilot site (at ~5 Ah / ~18.5 Wh per cell, 200k cells ≈ 3.7 MWh/yr, i.e. well under 0.01 GWh), so nameplate_capacity_gwh is left null. Status set to operational: HQ operational since 2021 and Eagle pilot line inaugurated/ramping as of Feb 2026. Cell format left null — QS cells are flat multilayer solid-state units; not clearly one of prismatic/cylindrical/pouch. Coordinates left null (address is 1730 Technology Drive, San Jose CA 95110, but precise lat/long not sourced). End market EV (automotive focus). Cross-checked: quantumscape.com, businesswire, electrive, electrek. Confidence moderate: identity/chemistry/status well sourced; capacity genuinely null because this is pilot scale.

Single physical site in Jamestown, Chautauqua County, New York (137,000 sq ft former electronics plant on a 52-acre campus). Announced Oct 2022 (Governor Hochul / Empire State Development). Battery SYSTEM / pack assembly began operating April–May 2025; lithium-ion CELL and module manufacturing is still being built out (over $40M of capital equipment ordered, backed by a ~$51M EXIM direct loan). Commercial cell production was guided for mid-2026 in early-2025 releases, but the most recent SEC 6-K filings pushed the target to "early FY2027" (Electrovaya's fiscal year ends 30 Sept, so ~late 2026). Hence status recorded as under_construction for the cell-manufacturing portion, and is_cell_manufacturer=true (a lithium-ion cell gigafactory in buildout; currently only pack/system assembly is live). Capacity: company guidance is "over 1 GWh" — phrased loosely as production "over the next five years", so the annual nameplate figure is ambiguous; recorded 1.0 GWh (ref year 2027) with low confidence and no clean phased ramp available. Chemistry: lithium-ion NMC with proprietary ceramic separator (Infinity platform). End markets: industrial/commercial EV (e-forklifts, e-trucks, e-buses, e-robots) plus stationary energy storage (ESS) — recorded as mixed. Coordinates not confirmed to plant level, left null. Cell format not confirmed, left null. Sources: Electrovaya press release "Start of Battery System Manufacturing in Jamestown, NY" (~May 2025); Governor Hochul / ESD gigafactory announcement (Oct 2022); Electrovaya FY2025/FY2026 SEC 6-K filings. WebFetch was blocked (403) on several domains; details drawn from search snippets across these sources.

Factorial Energy's solid-state battery development and pilot production facility in Methuen, Massachusetts. Announced Aug 2022, officially opened 23 Oct 2023. Described as the largest solid-state battery assembly line in the US, with annual capacity of up to 200 MWh (0.2 GWh/yr) — a pilot/pre-commercial scale line, not a mass-scale gigafactory. ~$50m investment, ~150 jobs. Genuinely manufactures cells: uses proprietary FEST (Factorial Electrolyte System Technology) solid electrolyte, scaled in 100+Ah cells compatible with existing Li-ion equipment; first phase included the cathode coating line with cell/testing equipment following. End market is EV (backed by investors Mercedes-Benz, Stellantis, Hyundai-Kia — investors, not JV partners, so not recorded as JV). Cell format recorded as pouch based on large-format FEST cell descriptions; not explicitly confirmed as pouch in the opening release, moderate confidence. Coordinates are city-level for Methuen, MA (exact plant address not confirmed to street level). No phased capacity ramp published, so capacity_by_year_json left null.

plant_name: Solid Power Louisville EV Cell Pilot Line
research_notes: Solid Power's Louisville, Colorado site (486 S. Pierce Ave, Louisville, CO 80027) is the company headquarters and home to its all-solid-state EV cell pilot production line, installed and operational since June 2022. It produces large-format, sulfide-based all-solid-state cells (silicon anode) designed at 60-100 Ah, "EV-scale". At full capacity the pilot line is expected to make ~300 cells/week (~15,000 cells/year) — this is an R&D/pilot line, NOT a commercial gigafactory, so no meaningful annual GWh nameplate figure exists; nameplate_capacity_gwh left null rather than guessed. It genuinely manufactures cells (not just materials/packs), hence is_cell_manufacturer=true. Cells are supplied to partners Ford and BMW for automotive qualification testing. Note: Solid Power also operates a SEPARATE electrolyte production facility ("SP2") in Thornton, CO (sulfide solid electrolyte, ~30 t/yr expanding to ~140 t/yr by 2028 via a 2024 US DOE $50m grant) — that Thornton site is a materials plant, not this Louisville cell line, and should not be conflated. Cell format recorded as pouch (large-format) with moderate confidence; coordinates left null to avoid guessing precise site location. Announced_year 2021 reflects when silicon cells transitioned to the pilot line; start_year 2022 is EV cell line installation. Sources: Solid Power GlobeNewswire release (2022-06-06); Electrek (2022-06-06); Denver Gazette (2022-06-06); Colorado Sun (2024-09-25) on the separate Thornton electrolyte expansion.

chemistry: silicon-anode lithium-ion (100% active silicon anode, 3D cell architecture)
research_notes: Enovix's original Fab-1 silicon-anode Li-ion cell production line at its Fremont, CA HQ (3501 W. Warren Avenue, Fremont, CA 94538). Shipped first commercial cells June 2022. Small-format cells for consumer electronics (wearables, smartphones, IoT). Reported nameplate ~254 MWh/yr (~0.25 GWh) at ~45 million cells/yr per 2021 SEC filing — small pilot/commercial scale, not gigafactory scale; capacity figure has moderate confidence. In Oct 2023 Enovix refocused the Fremont facility from a manufacturing hub into a "Center for Innovation" (new-product development). Under the 2024 restructuring plan (announced May 2024), Fab-1 R&D/pilot line equipment was relocated to Fab2 in Penang, Malaysia between May and July 2024; high-volume manufacturing now sits in Malaysia (Fab2) and an acquired facility in South Korea. Fremont remains the corporate HQ and R&D/innovation center, so status recorded as operational but as an R&D/innovation site rather than a volume cell factory. Coordinates left null (not sourced precisely). NOT a JV. Sources: Enovix 10-K (filed 2025-02-25); Enovix news releases and prnewswire (facility equipping 2021, Fab-1 commercial shipments 2022, Malaysia Fab2 opening/shipments 2024).

Amprius Technologies' HQ, R&D lab and in-house silicon-nanowire-anode (SiMaxx) cell manufacturing line at 1180 Page Avenue, Fremont, CA 94538. This IS a battery cell manufacturer (high-energy silicon-anode Li-ion pouch cells; the anode is the differentiator, cathode conventional). Operational: in Dec 2023 Amprius held a ribbon-cutting for a "10X capacity expansion", moving its proprietary anode/cell line from kWh to MWh scale; a May 2024 release cites ramping the SiMaxx mass-production tool to ~2 MWh capacity — hence nameplate ~0.002 GWh/yr (2024), pilot/small-commercial scale. IMPORTANT scoping caveat: Amprius's frequently-quoted 800 MWh SiCore pouch capacity and 1+ GWh cylindrical capacity are CONTRACT-MANUFACTURING partners (largely in Asia), NOT the Fremont site — they must not be attributed to this physical plant. A separately announced Amprius gigafactory in Brighton, Colorado is also a different site. End market is primarily aviation/eVTOL, UAV/drones, defence and light EVs (recorded as 'mixed'). Coordinates are an approximate geocode of the confirmed HQ street address. start_year 2023 reflects commissioning of the MWh-scale proprietary line (the Fremont lab has produced silicon-anode cells at smaller scale since c.2018). Capacity figure and precise nameplate carry moderate uncertainty; the fact that the site manufactures cells and is operational is well confirmed.

Natron Energy's Holland, Michigan sodium-ion battery cell plant at 70 W. 48th Street, Holland, MI 49423 (coordinates from mapping sources). A retrofit of a former Clarios battery facility. Began commercial-scale sodium-ion production in April/May 2024 - billed as the first commercial-scale sodium-ion battery production in the US. Chemistry: Prussian blue sodium-ion cells; end market is stationary/backup power for data centres, telecom and industrial (ESS). Reported full capacity was 600 MW of batteries per year - a POWER rating, not an annual GWh/year energy figure; I could not reliably convert to GWh/year, so nameplate_capacity_gwh is left null (do not confuse the North Carolina project's separate 24 GWh/yr figure with this site). IMPORTANT STATUS CAVEAT: Natron Energy permanently ceased all operations effective 3 September 2025 due to lack of funding, permanently closing the Holland plant (WARN notice, ~37 layoffs at Holland) and its Santa Clara, CA site, and halting the planned $1.4bn North Carolina gigafactory. Status recorded as 'operational' because the site did reach commercial operation, but it is now permanently shut. announced_year (2023) is approximate/inferred. Sources: Natron press releases via BusinessWire (28 Apr 2024), Green Car Congress (1 May 2024), Wikipedia, ess-news.com and Manufacturing Dive (Sep 2025 closure), WGVU News, Michigan LEO WARN notice (Aug 2025).

jv_partners: General Motors (GM Ventures) - cell supplier/strategic partner
research_notes: NOT a cell manufacturer — out of scope for a battery-cell database. Announced 9 July 2026, this 183,000 sq ft facility in Sacramento's Metro Air Park (near Sacramento International Airport) is a grid-scale battery ENERGY STORAGE SYSTEM (BESS) assembly/integration plant, billed as "America's first factory dedicated to grid-scale sodium-ion energy storage systems." It integrates sodium-ion CELLS manufactured by General Motors (June 2026 GM Ventures partnership: "Peak will integrate GM sodium-ion battery cells into its energy storage systems") into Peak's passively cooled storage platform — it does not itself manufacture cells. Capacity: up to 4 GWh of battery storage systems per year (system output, not cell output). Investment up to ~$71m; ~239 jobs; >6 GWh of customer commitments to 2030 (customers include Jupiter Power, RWE, Energy Vault). Shipments expected to begin Q1 2027. Status recorded as announced (site selection/fit-out stage, not confirmed under construction). Chemistry sodium-ion; end market grid ESS. Precise coordinates not sourced (Metro Air Park approx. only) so left null. Corroborating sources: pv-magazine-usa (2026-07-13), ess-news, Canary Media, Batteries International, Solar Power World (GM cell partnership, 2026-06). Confidence lowered because the site is pack/system integration rather than cell manufacturing.

Eos Energy's flagship manufacturing plant in Turtle Creek, PA (greater Pittsburgh). Manufactures zinc-based battery cells/modules (aqueous zinc "Znyth" chemistry, Eos Z3 system) for long-duration stationary energy storage (grid/ESS) - non-lithium, non-precious-earth. This is a genuine cell manufacturer, so is_cell_manufacturer=true. Status operational: commercial production launched on the first fully automated line on 1 July 2024. Capacity: the first automated line is rated ~1.25 GWh/year (recorded as nameplate_capacity_gwh for this site, ref year 2024); Turtle Creek is designed to house Line 1 and Line 2. Under "Project AMAZE" (American Made Zinc Energy, backed by a ~$303.5m DOE Loan Programs Office guarantee), Eos plans to scale to 8 GWh of total annual capacity by ~2026-2027, but that 8 GWh is spread ACROSS MULTIPLE SITES (Turtle Creek plus new lines at Duquesne, PA and a new 432,000 sq ft facility in Marshall Township / "Thorn Hill"), so the 8 GWh figure must NOT be attributed to Turtle Creek alone. Plans mention raising each Turtle Creek line from ~1.2 GWh to ~2 GWh; Turtle Creek's own eventual nameplate is therefore roughly 2.5-4 GWh but not cleanly sourced, so the confirmed operational 1.25 GWh line-1 figure is used. Coordinates left null - no sourced plant-specific lat/long (Turtle Creek borough is ~40.41N, -79.82W). Cross-checked across GlobeNewswire company release, Utility Dive, Solar Power World, Pennsylvania Business Report and Allegheny Front.

ESS Tech, Inc. (NYSE: GWH) manufactures long-duration iron flow batteries (iron and saltwater electrolyte) at its Wilsonville, Oregon plant — its sole manufacturing site and HQ. Qualifies as a cell/battery manufacturer (flow battery stacks/energy warehouses), not pack-only assembly. Status operational: still running per FY2025 results announced 5 March 2026 (net loss $63.4m for 2025). The plant nearly closed end-May 2025 amid a financing crisis (SEC 8-K warned of shutdown within days) but received emergency capital and continued operating. Capacity: installed automated line reached ~800 MWh/yr by end-2022 (energy-storage.news); a Feb 2025 pv-magazine/ess-news article describes nameplate at 'just shy of a gigawatt-hour' per year with potential to expand to ~6 GWh at the site — hence nameplate ~1.0 GWh/yr, capacity_ref_year 2025. Capacity figures are annual production nameplate. start_year ~2021 (automated line commissioned; company went public via SPAC Oct 2021). Coordinates left null (facility at 26440 SW Parkway Ave, Wilsonville OR 97070; exact decimal coords not sourced). Cell format 'mixed'/N/A — flow batteries do not use conventional prismatic/cylindrical/pouch cells. Additional sources: energy-storage.news 'iron flow battery firm ESS Inc ends 2022 with 800MWh production capacity'; businesswire FY2025 results 20260305499859; pv-magazine-usa.com/2025/02/13/go-with-the-flow-batteries. Moderate confidence: capacity from reputable trackers/news, not company nameplate spec sheet.

Form Factory 1, Weirton, West Virginia (55-acre former Weirton Steel site). Form Energy's first high-volume plant, ~550,000 sq ft, manufacturing the company's proprietary iron-air (iron, water and air) battery CELLS optimised for 100-hour long-duration grid storage (ESS). Announced Dec 2022; trial production Sep 2024; commercial production began 2025. Expansion underway (to ~850,000 sq ft by end-2025, ~1m sq ft and 750+ jobs by 2028). Nearly 400 employees as of early 2026. Total investment ~US$760m (public + private).

CAPACITY CAVEAT: Company states a production-capacity TARGET of "at least 500 MW of batteries per year by 2028" — this is power (MW), the metric Form uses, NOT an energy (GWh) figure. nameplate_capacity_gwh = 50 is a DERIVED estimate: 500 MW x 100-hour duration = 50 GWh of storage manufactured per year. This conversion is inferred, not a directly sourced GWh figure, and is a 2028 target (capacity_ref_year 2028), so confidence on the GWh number is low. Current 2025/2026 output is below this. If a GWh figure is not acceptable as derived, treat nameplate as null.

Coordinates left null (exact plant coordinates not confirmed by a source; site is the former Weirton Steel mill, Weirton, WV). cell_format null — iron-air modules are not standard Li-ion prismatic/cylindrical/pouch formats. Confidence 0.7: status, chemistry, location and the 500 MW/2028 target are well sourced across multiple outlets; the GWh conversion and exact dates are weaker.

Ambri (founded 2010 by Donald Sadoway et al., Marlborough, Massachusetts) develops grid-scale Liquid Metal batteries using calcium-antimony electrode chemistry — a molten-metal cell, not lithium-ion. The Marlborough site is a genuine cell manufacturing/testing facility: Ambri manufactures and tests the cells for its prototype and containerised commercial systems there (built a 432-cell beta prototype in a container), so is_cell_manufacturer = true. End market is long-duration grid/industrial energy storage (ESS), not EV. Cell format is a proprietary liquid-metal cell — none of the standard prismatic/cylindrical/pouch categories apply, so left null.

Status: Ambri ribbon-cut a production facility in Marlborough and achieved UL cell certification; classified operational, but with caveats — the company filed Chapter 11 in May 2024 and emerged from restructuring in Aug 2024 (as Ambri LLC), which adds uncertainty about current output. Hence moderate confidence (0.55).

Capacity NOT recorded as nameplate_capacity_gwh: the only figure found is a TARGET of "1 GW of battery units per year" for the FIRST PHASE of a full-scale plant, aimed at Q3 2025. That is (a) a power figure (GW), not annual energy throughput (GWh/year); (b) a forward target predating/around the bankruptcy; and (c) not a confirmed nameplate. Per the no-guessing rule, capacity fields left null rather than converting or assuming.

announced_year 2022 reflects the ~2022 'Innovation Hub' Massachusetts manufacturing-expansion announcement; treat as approximate. Coordinates left null — could not confirm the specific plant address (some sources also reference a separate Milford, MA facility), so no coordinate invented. Sources: Wikipedia 'Ambri Inc.'; IEEE Spectrum 'A Liquid Metal Battery for Grid Storage Nears Production'; ess-news (Aug 2024 restructuring); Worcester Business Journal; Utility Dive (Xcel 300 kWh pilot).

Statevolt (founder/CEO Lars Carlstrom, also behind the collapsed Britishvolt and Italvolt ventures) announced a $4bn, 54 GWh lithium-ion battery gigafactory in April 2022 and acquired a 135-acre site near the Salton Sea in Imperial Valley, California in January 2023. Intended to make cells for EVs and stationary storage (mixed end market), sourcing lithium and geothermal power from Controlled Thermal Resources' Hell's Kitchen project under an LOI (a supply relationship, not a manufacturing JV, so jv_partners left null). Original target was groundbreaking in 2024 and first production ~2025, but there is no credible confirmation of genuine construction start or operation; status kept as 'announced' given the developer's track record and lack of verified progress. Specific chemistry (LFP vs NMC), cell format, precise site coordinates, and phased ramp were not disclosed in available sources, so left null. Capacity of 54 GWh (full nameplate) corroborated across multiple sources (pv magazine, Charged EVs, Green Car Congress, Batteries News); reference year not specified. Confidence lowered due to project-viability uncertainty. Sources: pv-magazine-usa (2023-01-24), Charged EVs, Green Car Congress (2023).

Lyten's original San Jose, California facility is a semi-automated pilot/small-scale plant operating since May 2023. It produces cathode active material (CAM), lithium-metal anodes, AND NDAA-compliant lithium-sulfur battery cells on site, so it qualifies as a cell manufacturer (pilot scale). Chemistry is lithium-sulfur (Lyten's core technology). Capacity is uncertain: Lyten stated in Feb 2025 a plan to invest ~$20M and expand to deliver "up to 200 MWh per year" (0.2 GWh) at full capacity, but sources attribute this 200 MWh target inconsistently — sometimes to San Jose alone, sometimes to San Jose plus the San Leandro (ex-Cuberg/Northvolt) plant combined. Recorded 0.2 GWh nameplate with reduced confidence for this reason; true current output is likely well below that. Cell formats reported for Lyten include cylindrical and pouch (mixed). End markets span EV, defense/aerospace and drone applications (mixed). Lyten's large-scale manufacturing is planned elsewhere: a ~10 GWh gigafactory near Reno, Nevada (Phase 1 ~2027) and the San Leandro conversion — these are SEPARATE sites, not this San Jose row. No exact street address/coordinates confirmed, so lat/long left null. source_date reflects access date (2026-07-19); underlying facts drawn from Lyten/Cuberg announcements Nov 2024 and Feb 2025.

SES AI's Woburn, MA site is the company's global headquarters and human R&D centre, home to its "Electrolyte Foundry" and the Molecular Universe (AI4Science) effort, developing high-energy lithium-metal (Li-Metal) batteries for EV, UAM and other applications. It is NOT a commercial gigafactory: SES AI's actual Li-Metal cell production runs at SES Shanghai Giga (Jiading, Shanghai, ~300,000 sq ft, pilot-scale, cited elsewhere as ~1 GWh) and at a converted line in Chungju, South Korea (the world's first UAM-dedicated Li-Metal line, FAT completed Aug 2024). No sourced annual GWh nameplate capacity exists for the Woburn site, so nameplate_capacity_gwh is null. is_cell_manufacturer set false because Woburn is HQ/R&D/electrolyte production rather than a commercial cell-manufacturing plant (though prototype/R&D cell work occurs there). Chemistry is lithium-metal (Li-Metal anode); SES cells are large-format pouch (e.g. 50Ah/100Ah). Coordinates left null (not verified to source). Status "operational" reflects the site functioning as an active R&D/HQ facility. Confidence moderate: role and location well-sourced, but no capacity/coordinate data. Sources: ses.ai/about; SES AI UAM facility announcement (Chungju, S. Korea), 2024-08-12; SES Shanghai Giga descriptions.

24M Technologies (founded 2010) is a Cambridge, Massachusetts battery technology developer and licensor best known for its SemiSolid electrode process, plus Impervio separator, Eternalyte electrolyte and ETOP (Electrode-to-Pack) architecture. Its Cambridge site is primarily an HQ + R&D and pilot/demo cell manufacturing operation, not a large-scale gigafactory. It genuinely produces battery cells: a small pilot line (~100 MWh scale) ran cells from ~2018; as of mid-2025 the company reported a ~140,000 sq ft facility 'near Cambridge' scaling toward ~200 MWh/year (0.2 GWh/yr) of SemiSolid cell production. Nameplate figure (0.2 GWh/yr, 2025 ref) taken from mid-2025 reporting of the build-out; treat as pilot/demo scale. Cell format recorded as pouch based on SemiSolid cell format norms but not independently confirmed — moderate confidence. End market is mixed (EV, ESS/residential storage, consumer, and defense). Much of 24M's volume is via licensees (e.g. Kyocera in Japan, Rayong Thailand facility ~100 MWh) which are separate physical sites and not counted here. Exact street address/coordinates of the Cambridge-area plant not confirmed, so lat/long left null. Businesswire source (2025-09-30 ETOP announcement) returned HTTP 403 on direct fetch; details corroborated via search summaries of that release and prior 24M/MIT coverage.

UNIGRID (UC San Diego spin-off, founded 2021) is developing a Low-Rate Initial Production (LRIP) sodium-ion cell line at a new 12,000 sq ft facility in Sorrento Valley, San Diego, funded by a $2.9M California Energy Commission RAMP grant (announced June 2025) for design, build-out and validation. This is a pilot/LRIP line producing MWh-scale quantities of sodium-ion cells annually — NOT a gigafactory. UNIGRID deliberately uses a fabless/foundry model: the bulk of its cell manufacturing is contracted to foundries in China, Korea and Japan (~200 MWh/yr in 2025, targeting ~1 GWh/yr in 2026 and 2 GWh/yr by 2027 via those partners — capacity that is NOT located in San Diego). The San Diego site itself does manufacture cells (LRIP), so is_cell_manufacturer=true, but no GWh-scale nameplate figure is sourced for it, hence nameplate left null. Chemistry is proprietary NCO sodium-ion; end market primarily residential/ESS. No exact address/coordinates confirmed (Sorrento Valley, San Diego only). Status set to under_construction as the June 2025 grant funds building/validating the line; whether the LRIP line is fully operational by mid-2026 is not explicitly confirmed. Other sources: sodiumbatteryhub.com (2025-06-02, 2025-06-06), ess-news.com (2025-10-29), prnewswire.com foundry-10x release, energy-storage.news commercial shipments (Jan 2026).

Inlyte Energy is a US (San Francisco Bay Area) startup making sodium metal chloride / iron-sodium batteries for stationary storage (grid + data centre / AIDC). It genuinely manufactures cells and modules (not just packs), so is_cell_manufacturer=true; chemistry is sodium metal chloride (Na/FeCl2, "iron-sodium"), a niche non-lithium chemistry.

LOCATION UNCERTAIN: the specific "Hayward, CA" siting could not be confirmed. Public sources place Inlyte's HQ/registered addresses variously at San Leandro, Berkeley, San Francisco and Walnut Creek (Bay Area). Its main pilot cell/module line is near Derby, UK (a facility inherited from the 2022 Beta Research acquisition, ~10 MWh/yr). Reporting also references a small US pilot line (~5 MWh/yr) with a commercial US line design of ~500 MWh/yr. No source ties any of these figures specifically to a Hayward site, so nameplate left null and coordinates left null.

CAPACITY CONTEXT (not assigned to this row to avoid mixing sites/statuses): UK pilot ~10 MWh/yr; US pilot ~5 MWh/yr; planned first US commercial facility ~2 GWh/yr targeted for 2027 production, in partnership with HORIEN Salt Battery Solutions — but that commercial site was still under selection in 2026 and is not confirmed to be Hayward. Treat this row as a pilot/HQ cell-making site; confidence kept low (0.3) due to unconfirmed location and identity. Sources: pv magazine USA (2025-03-27), energy-storage.news (2025-12), ess-news.com (2026-05).

Coreshell is a Bay Area battery start-up commercialising a lithium-ion cell that uses an anode made from 100% domestically-sourced metallurgical silicon (MG-Si). It genuinely manufactures full cells, not just anode material: in late 2024 it unveiled the first commercial-scale 60 Ah cells and in 2025 began production at a newly-built 4 MWh/year facility in San Leandro, California, delivering A-samples to global automakers. The 4 MWh figure (=0.004 GWh/yr) is a small pilot/early-commercial line, confirmed by multiple reputable sources (PRNewswire, ChargedEVs, EV Engineering). Cells are built on standard equipment from South Korea's TopMaterial. Cathode chemistry not disclosed (likely NMC); cell format (60 Ah) not clearly stated as pouch/prismatic, left null. A separate, much larger 100 MWh facility is in the site-selection/design phase as of 2025 — that is a DIFFERENT future site, not this one, so its capacity is excluded here. Exact street address/coordinates not published; left null rather than guessed.

Zeta Energy (founded 2014, HQ Houston, Texas) is a lithium-sulfur battery developer. Its Houston site is its headquarters, R&D laboratory and PILOT-SCALE manufacturing facility — equipped for vapor deposition, powder prep, pyrolysis, slurry prep and coating, cell assembly, formation and cycling. It assembles lithium-sulfur cells (currently supplying pilot sample cells to partners), so it qualifies as a cell manufacturer, but it is NOT a commercial gigafactory. No GWh nameplate capacity has ever been published for this site — kept null rather than guessed. Cell format inferred as pouch (typical for Li-S; not explicitly sourced — treat as low-confidence). Status set to operational because the R&D/pilot line is running and producing sample cells; there is no announced commercial-scale plant here. Stellantis signed a joint DEVELOPMENT agreement with Zeta in Dec 2024 (batteries targeted for Stellantis EVs by 2030), but that is a technology partnership, not a JV manufacturing site, so jv_partners left null. Zeta has publicly stated it intends to scale via existing manufacturing partners rather than build its own large gigafactory. Coordinates left null (no confirmed street address). Confidence 0.5 given absence of capacity data and pilot/R&D nature. Other sources: Stellantis press release (stellantis.com, 2024-12-10); energycapitalhtx.com Zeta-Stellantis coverage; chargedevs.com Li-S feature.

Wholly owned Ford subsidiary manufacturing LFP battery cells in Marshall, Michigan; the first Ford-owned LFP cell plant and first automaker-owned LFP cell production in the US. NOT a JV: CATL is only a technology licensor and contracted service provider (licensing manufacturing process, cell chemistry and product design), not an owner or operator - so no jv_partners entry. LFP cell production began June 2026 (first US automotive LFP cells), confirmed by Ford newsroom and electrive/Reuters coverage. Nameplate capacity ~20 GWh/yr, scaled down from the original ~40 GWh plan announced Feb 2023; ~1,700 jobs at full ramp (500+ hired as of June 2026). Announced February 2023 (~$3.5bn investment). End market is primarily EV (initial batteries for Ford EVs); Ford has also announced expanding output to energy storage systems (ESS) at the site, so end market may become mixed over time. Cell format not confirmed by a source (CATL LFP is typically prismatic) - left null. Coordinates given are Marshall town centre (sourced); actual facility sits ~west of Marshall, south of I-94 on the MAJOR Campus (500 acres) - treat as approximate. Corroborating sources: Ford fromtheroad newsroom (2023, 2025, 2026), electrive.com (2026-06-18), wwmt.com (ESS expansion), choosemarshall.com.

Dragonfly Energy operates a domestic lithium battery cell manufacturing pilot line at its Reno, Nevada facility (in operation since the site opened; company founded 2012, cell pilot line completed July 2023). It genuinely manufactures cells (not just packs): the company uses its patented dry-electrode/dry-deposition process to make UL-listed cylindrical LiFePO4 (LFP) cells; the process is also claimed capable of NMC and LCO chemistries. Nameplate: the pilot line can produce up to ~150 MWh/year (0.15 GWh/yr) of LFP cells at 70% efficiency (company figure, 2023) — this is pilot/small commercial scale, not a gigafactory; no larger GWh capacity target has been publicly quantified, though the company says it can add production lines to scale. Dragonfly also runs a large battery pack/Battle Born Batteries assembly operation at the same Reno site, but the cell-manufacturing line is the relevant cell activity. End market: deep-cycle storage for RV, marine, off-grid and industrial/ESS plus consumer, so classed as mixed. Received Nevada Tech Hub funding (2024 and a $527k 2026 award) for battery R&D/advanced manufacturing. Coordinates not confirmed from a source, left null. Capacity is single-source (company) and refers to a pilot line, hence confidence 0.75.

Nanotech Energy's "Chico 2" is a ~50,000 sq ft graphene-based lithium-ion cell plant at the Chico Technology Center, Chico, California (near Chico Municipal Airport). Refurbishment began Nov 2022; graphene cells entered full production in early 2024, so status = operational. Produces cylindrical cells: 18650 from 2024, adding 21700 in 2025, at a design rate of 30,000 cells/day. Cells use Nanotech's proprietary non-flammable electrolyte and graphene electrodes (partners incl. Soteria current collectors, Rockwell Automation for automation) targeting consumer electronics, e-bikes and ESS (end_market = mixed). Capacity is reported by the company only as "150MW" — the unit is ambiguous (MW vs MWh/yr). Interpreted as ~150 MWh/year ≈ 0.15 GWh/yr (roughly consistent with 30,000 x ~11 Wh 18650 cells/day), hence moderate confidence on the capacity figure. No exact street address or coordinates were sourced, so lat/long left null (Chico city is ~39.73N, -121.84W but the precise site was not confirmed). NOTE: distinct from Nanotech's separate planned gigafactories — a 517-acre Tahoe-Reno/Nevada campus (2.5 GWh scaling toward 15 GWh) and a stated 6 GWh US brownfield search — which are different physical sites and not merged here. Sources: Nanotech/PRNewswire "confirms launch of 150MW production plant Chico 2" (Jan 2024), Design 2 Part Magazine (2024-02-08), graphene-info, and nanotechenergy.com facility pages. Company/single-source basis with unit ambiguity → confidence 0.55.

Sakuu Corporation (formerly Keracel), headquartered in San Jose, California. The "Silicon Valley" site is a ~79,000 sq ft battery printing, engineering and R&D hub opened August 2022, housing a pilot line for solid-state / lithium-metal cells produced via the Kavian 3D-printing platform (later a dry-process line). It qualifies as a cell manufacturer but at PILOT/pre-commercial scale — Sakuu claims to have produced 3D-printed battery cells here. No sourced annual GWh nameplate exists for this specific site, so nameplate_capacity_gwh is left null. The widely cited 60 GWh (by 2028) and 200 GWh (by 2030) targets refer to FUTURE, separate planned gigafactories (Porsche Consulting engaged to plan them), NOT this pilot facility — do not attach those figures to this row. Chemistry: solid-state, lithium-metal; cells are custom 3D-printed shapes so no standard cell_format. End market primarily EV. SK On signed a joint development agreement (July 2024) to industrialise the dry-process Kavian platform, but this is a JDA/licensing relationship, not a JV owning this site, so jv_partners left null. Coordinates left null (no precise sourced address). Company reported a dry-process cell durability breakthrough in Nov 2025 and was upgrading/auctioning surplus equipment in mid-2025; facility appears to remain operational. Confidence moderate-low because capacity and exact status of the pilot line are not precisely sourced.
